official.tuition_coverage_note: Successful scholarship applicants are automatically awarded a RTP Fees-Offset (Domestic) Scholarship (domestic students) or a Tuition Fee Scholarship (international students) which covers tuition fees for up to four years. The Entitlements Easy Guide states the scholarship provides a fee waiver for four years (full time) for doctoral candidates, and that if you have not completed in four years you will be required to pay tuition fees.
benefits: Annual stipend $35,500 (indexed) (2026 rate) for three years, with a possible six month extension
Tuition fees for up to four years, via an automatic RTP Fees-Offset (Domestic) Scholarship for domestic students or a Tuition Fee Scholarship for international students
Relocation allowance of $505 per eligible adult and $255 per eligible child, up to an absolute maximum of $1,455
Thesis allowance up to $840 for a doctoral thesis (proofreading or editing)

Paid leave of absence: 20 working days paid annual leave each year, 10 working days paid sick leave each year plus 60 working days over the life of the award, paid parental leave (100 working days primary carer, 20 working days secondary carer) and 10 working days paid family and domestic violence leave each year
Fortnightly stipend payments of $1,360.70 (full time) or $680.35 (part time) paid through University payroll
eligibility: Meet the entry requirements for a PhD or Professional Doctorate as set out for the proposed program at Swinburne
Hold a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours (or equivalent)
Propose a research project that aligns with a Swinburne Research Strategy and Ecosystem area
Not be receiving another stipend scholarship to support general living costs if that stipend is greater than 75 per cent of the student's RTP Stipend or SUPRA scholarship stipend rate

Be applying for entry into a PhD or Professional Doctorate, or be currently enrolled in a Swinburne PhD or Professional Doctorate for less than two years at the closing date of the application round and have demonstrated outstanding progress, or have received an offer for candidature and not yet enrolled
Open to both domestic students (Australian citizen, New Zealand citizen or Australian permanent resident) and international students

Organise a minimum of two referees to complete a Swinburne Research referee report and have them email it directly to HDRrefereereports@swin.edu.au by the round deadline

Applicants for Doctor of Philosophy (Clinical Psychology) and Doctor of Psychology (Clinical and Forensic Psychology) must also organise two professional references, so a minimum of four reports in total

Meet Swinburne's English language requirements for postgraduate courses by research; evidence of meeting this requirement must be valid until the scholarship enrolment deadline (international and permanent resident applicants only)
Maintain satisfactory progress, with continuation of the award dependent on regular progress reports; the award terminates on submission of the thesis for examination

Certified academic transcripts and evidence of completion
Evidence of prior research including publications
Evidence of meeting the English language requirements for Swinburne postgraduate courses by research (international and permanent resident applicants only)

Research and publication experience relative to opportunity

official.application_route: Apply online through Swinburne's higher degree by research application while a scholarship round is open, selecting 'Swinburne Research Scholarships'; current PhD students use the separate current-student application form.
official.study_mode: Full-time. Part-time study may only be approved in exceptional circumstances, such as significant caring responsibilities or a medical condition, and the part-time stipend is 50 per cent of the full-time rate.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to both domestic students (Australian citizen, New Zealand citizen or Australian permanent resident) and international students.
official.international_eligibility: International students are eligible. Successful international scholarship applicants are automatically awarded a Tuition Fee Scholarship covering tuition fees for up to four years, and international offer holders must enrol by Tuesday 29 June 2027 for a Round 2 offer.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Eligible courses are the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) and Professional Doctorate only. The proposed research project must align with a Swinburne Research Strategy and Ecosystem area. Applications from Research Masters candidates are not currently being considered, with no provision to convert a doctoral offer to a Research Masters.
official.research_requirement: A completed HDR Research Proposal template signed by the nominated Principal Supervisor is required, and the quality and alignment of the proposal with Swinburne's Research Strategy and Ecosystem is assessed competitively. Applicants must also meet the required standards of achievement and research experience for entry into the proposed doctoral program.
official.duration: Three years of stipend at full-time load, with a possible six-month extension subject to satisfactory academic progress; tuition fees covered for up to four years for doctoral candidates.
official.description: Swinburne Research Stipend (SRS) scholarships are awarded to candidates of exceptional research potential undertaking doctoral studies, and the awards are provided to assist with general living costs. Research scholarships are available by application to both future and current students enrolled in or applying for a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or Professional Doctorate course at Swinburne, and successful applicants are automatically awarded a fees-offset or tuition fee scholarship covering tuition fees for up to four years.
official.program_type: University research scholarship for doctoral candidates (PhD / Professional Doctorate)
official.english_requirement: English language requirements for Swinburne postgraduate courses by research: IELTS (Academic Module) overall 6.5 with no individual band below 6.0; IELTS One Skill Retake on the same basis; PTE Academic 58 with no communicative skill less than 50; TOEFL iBT (Australia) 79 (no less than 13 in reading, 12 in listening, 18 in speaking, 21 in writing); Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 176 with no band less than 169. Michigan English Test (MET) and LanguageCert Academic are not applicable for postgraduate courses by research. Evidence must be valid until the scholarship enrolment deadline, and is required from international and permanent resident applicants only.

applicant_utility.summary: Swinburne's doctoral scheme pays a $35,500 tax-free annual stipend for three years, attaches a tuition fee waiver for up to four years (an RTP Fees-Offset for domestic applicants, a Tuition Fee Scholarship for international applicants), and adds a relocation allowance of $505 per adult and $255 per child up to $1,455 plus an $840 thesis editing allowance. There is no separate nomination step because every applicant is assessed automatically for both SUPRA and the RTP Stipend, so the real gate is getting a supervisor to sign your HDR Research Proposal before a round closes. The scheme only opens twice a year, and the official page currently reads 'Applications are closed' following the 9 October 2026 Round 2 deadline, so the practical move is to build supervisor contact and referee availability now rather than waiting for the next window.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral researchers holding a first-class honours degree or equivalent published output, whose project maps onto one of Swinburne's four research institutes and who can win a Principal Supervisor's commitment before a round closes.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach a prospective Principal Supervisor months before a round opens and get sections of the HDR Research Proposal template signed; Clinical Psychology and Doctor of Psychology applicants only complete sections A and B before interview, with the supervisor signing section C.

Line up at least two referees early and confirm they will email the completed Swinburne Research referee report straight to HDRrefereereports@swin.edu.au - for 2026 Round 2 that was due 16 October 2026, a week after the application itself closed.
Check your English test result will still be valid on the scholarship enrolment deadline (Tuesday 29 June 2027 for a Round 2 international offer), not merely on the day you submit.
Get academic transcripts certified and keep proof of citizenship or ID to hand, because incomplete applications may not be considered at all.
Budget separately for Overseas Student Health Cover, which the entitlements guide explicitly excludes, and for rent above what a $35,500 stipend covers in Melbourne.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting without a signed HDR Research Proposal - the template cannot be completed without the nominated Principal Supervisor's agreement.
Referee reports arriving late or reaching the Graduate Research Office by any route other than the referee's own email.
An English test result that lapses before the scholarship enrolment deadline.
Already holding a living-cost stipend worth more than 75 per cent of the SUPRA or RTP Stipend rate, which makes you ineligible outright.
Being more than two years into a Swinburne PhD at the closing date without demonstrated outstanding progress.
A project that does not clearly align with a Swinburne Research Strategy and Ecosystem area, since proposal alignment is an explicit competitive criterion.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Overseas Student Health Cover costs, which the Entitlements Easy Guide states are not covered; the shortfall between the $35,500 stipend and Melbourne rent and living costs; relocation costs above the $505 per adult / $255 per child allowance or for non-claimable items such as accommodation and meals in transit; and tuition fees for any candidature that runs beyond the four-year fee waiver.
document_audit: The HDR Research Proposal template must carry the nominated Principal Supervisor's signature - an unsigned or unfinished template is the single most likely reason an application is treated as incomplete.

Clinical Psychology and Doctor of Psychology applicants need two professional references in addition to at least two academic referees, so four reports in total; the same person may serve as both referee and professional reference if appropriate.

Only international and permanent resident applicants are asked for English evidence with the scholarship application, but all applicants still have to meet Swinburne's English language requirements for entry.

Relocation claims require original receipts within 6 months of starting the degree for the student and within 12 months for a spouse and children, and only air travel, car travel or removal expenses are claimable.

Thesis allowance claims need original receipts or invoices showing the business name and Australian Business Number, submitted within one year of thesis submission and no more than two years after the scholarship ends.

applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit the higher degree by research application online while a round is open with 'Swinburne Research Scholarships' selected, attach the signed proposal and all supporting documents, then have referees email their reports directly to the Graduate Research Office; outcomes are released progressively weeks after the round closes and offers must be accepted by the published enrolment date.
